q.t: What is the place value of 4 in 45,867?
q.e: 4 sits in the ten-thousands place, so it is worth 4 ten thousands = 40,000.

q.t: How many thousands make 10,000?
q.e: Every place is ten times the one on its right, so 10 thousands = 1 ten thousand.

q.t: Write ‘twenty-three thousand four hundred five’ in figures.
q.e: 23 thousands, then 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones — the 0 holds the empty tens place.

q.t: Which is the number name of 30,602?
q.e: Split at the comma: ‘30’ thousand, then ‘602’ = six hundred two.

q.t: Which is greater: 9,999 or 10,000?
q.e: 10,000 has five digits and 9,999 has only four — more digits means a bigger number.

q.t: Round 2,346 to the nearest ten.
q.e: The ones digit is 6 (5 or more), so 2,346 is nearer 2,350 than 2,340.

q.t: Which digit is in the hundreds place of 58,317?
q.e: From the right: 7 ones, 1 ten, 3 hundreds.

q.t: 10 hundreds make:
q.e: 10 × 100 = 1,000 — ten of a place make one of the next place to the left.

q.t: What is the smallest five-digit number?
q.e: The smallest five-digit number starts with 1 and has zeros after it.

q.t: What is the largest four-digit number?
q.e: Put the biggest digit, 9, in all four places. One more would need a fifth digit.

q.t: What number is 7,000 + 400 + 9?
q.e: 7 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones — a 0 keeps the empty tens place.

q.t: 52,038 = 5 ten thousands + 2 thousands + ___ hundreds + 3 tens + 8 ones. Fill the blank.
q.e: The hundreds digit of 52,038 is 0 — there are no hundreds.

q.t: Round 6,849 to the nearest hundred.
q.e: Look at the tens digit: 4 is less than 5, so round down to 6,800.

q.t: Round 7,512 to the nearest thousand.
q.e: Look at the hundreds digit: 5 means round up, so 7,512 → 8,000.
4,734 has only four digits; all the others have five.

q.t: Which of these is TRUE?
q.e: Count digits first: 9,990 has four digits, 49,014 has five, so 9,990 is smaller.

q.t: What is 1 more than 19,999?
q.e: Every place is full of 9s, so adding 1 carries all the way: 20,000.

q.t: What is 1,000 more than 38,950?
q.e: Only the thousands digit goes up by 1: 8 becomes 9.

q.t: In 55,000, what is the difference between the values of the two 5s?
What is 10 more than 9,995?
Using the digits 3, 0, 7, 1 and 9 once each, make the LARGEST five-digit number.
q.e: Put the biggest digit in the biggest place: 9, 7, 3, 1, 0.

q.t: Using the digits 3, 0, 7, 1 and 9 once each, make the SMALLEST five-digit number.
q.e: 0 cannot go first (it would not be five digits), so start with 1, then 0, 3, 7, 9.

q.t: Which number rounds to 2,400 at the nearest hundred?
q.e: The tens digit of 2,372 is 7 (5 or more), so it rounds up to 2,400. The others have tens digits below 5.

q.t: Which number rounds to 5,000 at BOTH the nearest hundred and the nearest thousand?
A book has about 250 pages and each page has about 40 words. About how many words are in the book?
q.e: Multiply instead of counting: 250 × 40 = 10,000.

q.t: A spacecraft travels at least 28,000 km in one hour. How do you read 28,000?
q.e: Split at the comma: ‘28’ thousand and ‘000’ — so twenty-eight thousand.

q.t: How many hundreds are there in 10,000?
q.e: 10 hundreds make 1,000, so 10 × 10 = 100 hundreds make 10,000.

q.t: What is the GREATEST number that rounds to 3,200 at the nearest ten?
q.e: 3,205 would round up to 3,210, so the biggest number still nearer 3,200 is 3,204.

q.t: What digit must go in the box so that 4▢,512 is greater than 48,900?
q.e: 48,512 is less than 48,900, so the thousands digit must be bigger than 8 — it must be 9.

q.t: Ravi says 9,990 is greater than 49,014 because 9 is greater than 4. Why is he wrong?
o: 49,014 has more digits, so it is bigger
You compare the last digits first
q.e: Count the digits first. A five-digit number is always bigger than a four-digit one.

q.t: A car’s meter reads 24,995 km. After 7 more km, what does it read (in km)?
Round 23,456 to the nearest hundred and also to the nearest thousand. How much bigger is the hundred answer?
q.e: Nearest hundred: 23,500 (tens digit 5). Nearest thousand: 23,000 (hundreds digit 4). Difference = 500.

q.t: Using 5, 2, 8, 0 and 6 once each, make the LARGEST five-digit ODD number.
q.e: An odd number must end in 5 here (the only odd digit). Arrange the rest biggest-first: 8, 6, 2, 0, then 5.

q.t: What is the smallest five-digit number with all its digits different?
q.e: Start with 1 (0 can’t go first), then use the smallest unused digits: 0, 2, 3, 4.

q.t: How many five-digit numbers are there in all (from 10,000 to 99,999)?
q.e: 99,999 − 10,000 = 89,999, and we add 1 to count both ends: 90,000.

q.t: A number has 6 ten thousands, 0 thousands and 4 hundreds. Its ones digit is 3 and its tens digit is twice the ones digit. What is the number?
q.e: Tens digit = 2 × 3 = 6, so the places read 6, 0, 4, 6, 3.

q.t: A shop says it had ‘about 4,000 visitors’, rounded to the nearest thousand. Which could be the real number?
q.e: 4,380 has hundreds digit 3, so it rounds down to 4,000. 4,620 and 4,500 round up to 5,000; 3,420 rounds to 3,000.

q.t: Count from 10,000 to 20,000 in steps of 1,000, saying both 10,000 and 20,000. How many numbers do you say?
q.e: 10 jumps of 1,000 make 10,000, but you say one more number than the jumps: 11.

q.t: A number rounded to the nearest ten is 7,490. What is the SMALLEST it could be?
q.e: 7,485 has ones digit 5, so it rounds up to 7,490. 7,484 would round down to 7,480.

q.t: Arrange 30,303; 33,003; 30,330; 33,030 from greatest to smallest. Which comes THIRD?
q.e: Order: 33,030 > 33,003 > 30,330 > 30,303. Compare from the left and stop at the first difference.
